'''''Aloina ambigua''''', commonly known as '''tall aloe-moss''', is a species of [[moss]] in the family [[Pottiaceae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Aloina ambigua |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/aloina-ambigua/ |website=britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk}}</ref> The species was frequently misidentified with ''[[Aloina aloides]]'' prior to publication of the book, ''Flora''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aloina aloides |url=https://cisfbr.org.uk/Bryo/Cornish_Bryophytes_Aloina_aloides_sstr.html |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=cisfbr.org.uk}}</ref> 

== Description ==
The leaves of ''Aloina ambigua'' exhibit a slight curl when dry, while they become long and spreading in moist conditions, measuring approximately 1.0–3.0 × 0.3–0.7 mm. They are lingulate in shape, with a base that is shortly sheathing and an apex that is cucullate, incurved, and approximately obtuse (or subacute when flattened). The spores measure 14–16 [[Micrometre|μm]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Aloina ambigua |url=https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora/species/aloina-ambigua/ |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Aloina ambigua |url=https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/site/assets/files/0/21/126/aloina-ambigua.pdf |website=nzpcn.org.nz}}</ref>

== Identification ==
[[File:Aloina ambigua (b, 153235-482344) 0913.JPG|thumb|Spores]]
In terms of size and growth habit, ''Aloina ambigua'' closely resembles ''[[Aloina aloides]]''. These plants can be found as solitary specimens or in patches that range from dark green to reddish-brown, typically reaching heights of 2–5 mm. The leaves exhibit a strong similarity to those of ''A. aloides''; however, the nerve generally terminates at the leaf tip and seldom extends beyond it. Capsules are prevalent during the winter and spring seasons, playing a crucial role in differentiating ''A. ambigua'' from ''A. aloides''. Identification based solely on field characteristics is usually not feasible without the presence of capsules. When mature, the capsules are typically upright or only slightly tilted, featuring a distinct membrane located between the capsule's opening and the peristome teeth. Additionally, the calyptra is devoid of hair.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Aloina ambigua {{!}} Tall Aloe-moss |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Aloina-ambigua.pdf |website=britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk}}</ref>

== Habitat ==
''Aloina ambigua'' is a lowland species, usually being found in thin, lime-rich soils like chalk and limestone. It typically thrives on exposed banks, rock ledges, cliffs, as well as in quarries, chalk pits, and sand pits. In contrast to ''A. aloides'', it seldom grows on mortar surfaces of walls.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Distribution of Aloina ambigua in Great Britain and Ireland |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Atlas-of-British-and-Irish-Bryophytes-V2-202.pdf |website=britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
''Aloina ambigua'' has been found in [[Europe]], [[North America]], [[North Africa]], [[Australia]] and [[New Zealand]].<ref name=":2" />
